title.narrative: Stöd till HBTQI+ i Bolivia "Diversidades en la diversidad"
support to LGBTIQ+ in Bolivia "Diversidades en la diversidad"

description.narrative:
Motiveringarna som driver detta förslag är att HBTQ rörelsen, civila samhället och befolkningsgrupper som representerar sexuell mångfald och dissidens i Bolivia, främst lesbiska, bisexuella och transpersoner är både diskriminerade, splittrade och har ingen relevant representation bland civila samhället för att kunna blir hörda i Bolivianska samhället. Samtidigt är dessa organisationer oartikulerade med varandra och från den breda kvinnorörelsen i Bolivia.
Förslaget är fokuserad på den dissidenta befolkningen eftersom den anser att deras större synlighet och närvaro är nödvändig för framtida HBTQ+ rörelsen i Bolivia. Framväxten av organiserade dissidenter är ett nytt fenomen i det bolivianska samhället, de är människor som inte befinner sig inom de binära paradigmerna sex och kön.
Det är viktigt att nämna att deras bidrag till debatterna och reflektionerna är relevanta till diskussionerna kring avkolonisering och avpatriarkalisering, som oundvikliga processer för att ompröva maktförhållanden och allianser och gå vidare till artikulationer om jämlikhet.
Projektet kommer att bidra till att bygga upp och stärka HBTQ rörelsen i Bolivia samt att stärka artikulering av olika organisationer från civila samhället som representerar HBTQ+ befolkning. Projektet syftar också till att stärka dessa organisationer för att bygga upp processer för avpatriarkalisering och avkolonisering, feministisk, sekulär, intersektionell och interkulturella proceser i Bolivia.
De förväntade resultat är: 1.Transkvinnor, lesbiska, dissidenta och icke-hegemoniska grupper deltar med jämlikhet i HBTQ+ rörelsen i Bolivia för att kunna utöva sina rättigheter. 2. HBTQ+ rörelsen i Bolivia genomför och utvecklar strategier för att bidra till avpatriarkalisering och avkolonisering i sina agendor. 3.HBTQ+ rörelse i Bolivia har en synlig representation av alla grupper och befolkningar på nationell nivå.
4.Feministisk och HBTQ+ rörelsen i Bolivia bygger mötesplatser för att stärka allianser för att påverka den politiska agendan.
Projektets totala budget är på 2 500 000 SEK. Organisationen (Colectivo Rebeldia) som kommer att genomföra projektet är en lokal NGO som har lång erfarenhet av att arbeta med kvinnors rättigheter, sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter, urbefolkningsrättigheter och HBTQ+ rörelser.

The motivations behind this proposal are that the LGBTQ movement, civil society and population groups representing sexual diversity and dissent in Bolivia, mainly lesbians, bisexuals and transgender people are both discriminated , divided and have no relevant representation among civil society in order to be heard in Bolivian society. At the same time, these organizations are unarticulated with each other and from the broad women's movement in Bolivia.
The proposal focuses on the dissident population as it considers that their greater visibility and presence is necessary for the future LGBTQ + movement in Bolivia. The emergence of organized dissidents is a new phenomenon in Bolivian society, they are people who are not within the binary paradigms of sex and gender.
It is important to mention that their contributions to the debates and reflections are relevant to the discussions on decolonization and depatriarchalisation, as inevitable processes for reconsidering power relations and alliances and moving on to articulations of equality.
The project will help to build and strengthen the LGBTQ movement in Bolivia and to strengthen the articulation of various civil society organizations that represent the LGBTQ + population. The project also aims to strengthen these organizations to build processes for de-patriarchalization and decolonization, feminist, secular, intersectional and intercultural processes in Bolivia.
The expected results are: Transgender women, lesbians, dissidents and non-hegemonic groups participate equally in the LGBTQ + movement in Bolivia in order to exercise their rights. 2. The LGBTQ + movement in Bolivia implements and develops strategies to contribute to de-patriarchalization and decolonization in its agendas. The LGBTQ + movement in Bolivia has a visible representation of all groups and populations at the national level. 4. The feminist and LGBTQ + movement in Bolivia is building meeting places to strengthen alliances to influence the political agenda.
The project's total budget is SEK 2,500,000. The organization (Colectivo Rebeldia) that will implement the project is a local NGO that has extensive experience of working with women's rights, sexual and reproductive health and rights, indigenous peoples' rights and LGBTQ + movements. The project aims to build and strengthen the LGBTQ movement in Bolivia and to strengthen the articulation of various civil society organizations that represent the LGBTQ population. The project also aims to strengthen these organizations to build processes for de-patriarchalization and decolonization, feminist, secular, intersectional and intercultural processes in Bolivia.

In 2024, the joint work with the organizations and collectives of the Working Group was strengthened, following up on actions resulting from the received support funds, sharing and disseminating actions with other networks, and attending those that it was possible to participate in. The strengthened capacities of organizations and collectives enable them to support their autonomies in presenting proposals and managing projects, emphasizing collective work, the importance of dialogues, and prioritizing political advocacy work in their territories. Concrete Examples of Strengthened Capacities in Action: Development and Submission of Project Proposals Several grassroots LGBTQ collectives, after participating in capacitybuilding workshops, were able to independently design and submit proposals to national or international funding sources. For example:A trans rights organization in Cochabamba submitted a successful proposal to a regional fund to implement a campaign on access to healthcare for trans women. An LGBTIQ youth collective in El Alto developed a community project focused on mental health support and was granted municipal funding for its implementation. Internal Governance and Strategic Planning Organizations reported greater clarity in roles, better internal communication, and improved decisionmaking structures.
A lesbianled feminist collective revised its statutes and incorporated an intersectional and intercultural approach into its strategic plan for 20252028. A rural LGBTQ group created an internal governance committee to ensure community participation in decisionmaking and transparency in the use of resources.
Political Advocacy and Local Influence Strengthened capacities allowed collectives to actively engage in advocacy and dialogue with public institutions. In Santa Cruz, an LGBTQ network held meetings with municipal authorities to advocate for the inclusion of sexual diversity in local education policies. In Potosí, a collective participated in a departmental forum on human rights and successfully pushed for the inclusion of LGBTQ issues in the agenda. Collective Actions and Movement Building Organizations began working more collaboratively, forming alliances for greater impact. Several groups coorganized a national campaign during Pride Month focusing on antidiscrimination and legal recognition of gender identity. A coalition of LGBTIQ collectives from different regions coordinated efforts to monitor human rights violations and publish a shadow report submitted to an international human rights mechanism. Creation of Local Agendas Using tools developed during the project, organizations created their own political and social agendas. In Tarija, a collective developed a fivepoint local agenda on health, education, security, political participation, and access to employment, which was presented to local candidates during municipal elections. In general, we can affirm that in this process of supporting organizations and collectives, has been very relevant for the local organizations.
In the second semester, the Fourth Working Group Meeting on Strengthening Diversities and Dissidences has been take place on November 15 and 16, 2024, in Santa Cruz, with the participation of two members per organization of the Working Group. A significant achievement has been the education and training of LGBTI individuals through academic courses conducted in collaboration with CESU at the University of San Simón.However, the most important results achieved are in the area of advocacy: Examples of Political Advocacy and Influence Results Inclusion of LGBTQ Rights in Local Policies: As a direct result of advocacy efforts supported by the project, some municipal governments in Bolivia have begun to incorporate LGBTQ rights and antidiscrimination measures into their local development plans or human rights policies. For example: The Santa Cruz municipal government adopted an antidiscrimination ordinance that includes protections based on sexual orientation and gender identity. The city of Cochabamba committed to implementing training for public servants on LGBTQ issues to improve access to public services. Participation in National Policy Dialogues: LGBTQ organizations strengthened through the project were invited to participate in national human rights forums and consultations related to gender and diversity. Their contributions influenced the language and priorities of policy documents. For example, the Ministry of Justice included inputs from the LGBTQ movement in drafting protocols for preventing discrimination in public institutions. Visibility and Public Recognition: The project helped raise the profile of LGBTQ issues in public debates and media, creating pressure for political change. Successful public campaigns organized by the collectives coincided with political commitments from candidates during election campaigns to support LGBTQ rights. Strategic Alliances for Legal Reform: The project facilitated alliances between LGBTQ groups and other human rights organizations, enabling stronger collective lobbying efforts for legal
reforms, such as advancing gender identity laws or antidiscrimination legislation. Increased Leadership in Political Spaces: Members of the supported organizations gained positions or influential roles in political or advisory bodies at local and national levels, enhancing the communitys voice in decisionmaking processes.
